route: 9 (response-frequency matching, raw labels vs live integers)
evidence: Item axis needs no route: the live item code IS the source .xlsx column header verbatim, e.g. '(FTND_4) How many cigarettes per day did you smoke?', so item_text is the header itself and a permutation is impossible. Option axis checked by counting every label in the CC0 deposit against every integer in the live table: all 16 item x level cells match exactly -- FTND_1 27/54/148/90 for resp 0/1/2/3 (After 60 minutes / 31 - 60 minutes / 6 - 30 minutes / Within 5 minutes), FTND_4 64/183/53/19 for 10 or less / 11 - 20 / 21 - 30 / 31 or more, FTND_2 170 No vs 149 Yes, FTND_3 111 Any other vs 208 The first one in the morning, FTND_5 181/138, FTND_6 126/193. Within every item the level counts are distinct, so each option_text is pinned to one resp value rather than only the scale direction. Re-runnable as verify_kushnir2017_ftnd.R (VERDICT: PASS).

Paper Table 3 publishes Mean+/-SD per numbered item for the same n=299 sample. Live per-item values reproduce all 12: MSPSS1 5.48/1.28 vs 5.48/1.28, MSPSS2 5.48/1.15 vs 5.48/1.15, MSPSS3 5.83/1.29, MSPSS4 5.34/1.46, MSPSS5 5.76/1.24, MSPSS6 5.25/1.22, MSPSS7 4.19/1.56, MSPSS8 5.03/1.32, MSPSS9 5.37/1.26, MSPSS10 5.55/1.37, MSPSS11 5.48/1.30, MSPSS12 4.78/1.33; largest deviation 0.0046 (mean) and 0.0040 (SD). This does NOT verify option_text<->resp: anchors 2-6 come from the canonical MSPSS form, with only the 1 = very strongly disagree / 7 = very strongly agree endpoints confirmed by the paper.

route: explicit code labels in the paper (S1 Table Q1..Q32) + route 1 (published age correlations reproduced) + route 7/8 (marker items Q26/Q27 floor; anxiety-fear and gender direction)
evidence: ITEM AXIS is a code-label match, not an inference: S1 Table prints every item as 'Q1. ...' .. 'Q32. ...', the SPSS deposit's columns are named Q1..Q32, and data/latifi_2026_insect_fear.py melts those columns by name with no rename, so 32/32 items are tied at the source and every item is distinguished from every other. RESP AXIS carried a decision and was checked numerically in verify_latifi_2026_insect_fear.R (VERDICT: PASS): under the shipped orientation (Q1-Q23 1=Strongly agree..5=Strongly disagree, Q24-Q32 1=Never..5=Always) the live table reproduces the paper's own published age correlations -- knowledge +0.100 vs published 0.10, insectophobia +0.034 vs 0.035, anxiety +0.074 vs 0.077, max deviation 0.003 -- whereas the deposit's labelled direction gives -0.100 and -0.034 for the first two; Q26 and Q27 sit at 77.2% and 89.2% on resp=1, fixing 'Never' at 1 for the frequency block; and cor(anxiety, insectophobia)=+0.442 with girls 3.409 > boys 2.974 on insectophobia, both of which invert under the labelled direction. What this does NOT establish: no statistical route here separates items WITHIN a block (e.g. Q5 from Q6); that rests entirely on the Q-code label match above, which is why the status is VERIFIED rather than PARTIAL.

route: route 3 (published by-sex totals + alpha) + route 7/8 (marker item SWLS5)
evidence: Route 3 (published totals, paper Table 2) + route 7/8 (marker item), all from irw_fetch. Males n=195: published 21.89 +/- 5.85, live 21.89 +/- 5.85 (diff +0.002 / +0.003). Females n=332: published 20.59 +/- 6.34, live 20.60 +/- 6.34 (diff +0.006 / +0.002). Cronbach alpha published .86, live .857. Direction control: reversing the 1-7 anchors gives a male mean of 18.11, off by 3.78, so 1=Strongly disagree..7=Strongly agree and the items are stored raw. Marker: SWLS5 has both the lowest mean (3.816 vs 3.877/4.078/4.636/4.670) and the largest SD (1.786 vs 1.408-1.535), the SWLS signature of item 5; the rival SWLS2<->SWLS5 swap is rejected because it would put canonical item 5 at mean 4.670, the scale maximum. NOT ESTABLISHED: SWLS1..SWLS4 are not separated from one another -- the paper publishes no per-item statistics, the workbook has no variable/value labels, all five items share one 1-7 scale and there is one unidimensional subscale with no reverse-keyed item, so routes 1, 2, 5 and 6 are unavailable; that assignment rests on the source column numbering matching canonical SWLS order. Also noted: the corrected item-total ordering (3 .765 > 1 .726 > 5 .680 > 4 .658 > 2 .548) does not match Diener 1985's (item 5 weakest), which is treated as a sample-level finding. Hence PARTIAL.
